cases.prompt: Our MQL to SQL conversion rate is 34%. Why did it jump from 21% last month?
cases.setup: The 34% is computed from current-stage counts. No stage history exists.
expect_pass: identifies that the figure is a snapshot ratio, not a conversion rate, because it divides two populations observed at the same instant
names the specific alternative explanation: the rate rises when the MQL stage drains, for example when top-of-funnel volume fell or sales worked through a backlog, with no conversion behaviour change
gives the cheap diagnostic: in a snapshot funnel the stage counts sum to the population, in a cohort funnel they do not
states what a cohort rate would need: fact_lead_stage with entry timestamps, and a declared conversion window
still reports what the snapshot is good for: where volume is sitting, capacity and coverage
expect_fail: explains the jump as improved conversion
refuses to engage with the number at all

cases.prompt: Break down our MQL to SQL drop-off by whether sales rejected the lead or never worked it.
cases.setup: No SAL acceptance event exists in the CRM: no status value, no task type, no timestamp.
expect_pass: returns unavailable for the rejected-versus-untouched split
names the missing instrumentation as the finding: SAL is not instrumented, which is why MQL-to-SQL looks noisy in this org
states that rejected and untouched have opposite fixes, so the blended rate averages two different problems
names the resolving change concretely: a lead status value or a task type logged on acceptance
offers the computable proxy with its bias named, for example leads with zero logged sales activity as a floor on untouched
expect_fail: computes a rejected-versus-untouched split from available fields without flagging that the distinction is not instrumented

cases.prompt: Conversion has fallen three months running: 18.2%, 15.1%, 11.4%. What's going wrong?
cases.setup: Median cycle is 90 days. The three cohorts are 120, 75 and 34 days old.
expect_pass: checks cohort age against the conversion window before diagnosing anything
states that only the first cohort is complete and the other two are truncated, so the sequence is not a decline
reports the two recent figures as lower bounds
offers the valid comparison: all three cohorts at a common day-30 horizon
does not silently drop the incomplete cohorts
expect_fail: diagnoses a conversion decline from the three figures
drops the incomplete cohorts and reports only 18.2%

cases.prompt: Our person-level MQL to opportunity rate is 4%. Industry benchmark is 25%. Are we that bad?
cases.setup: Enterprise B2B, average six contacts per opportunity.
expect_pass: flags the unit-of-analysis mismatch before accepting the comparison
states that a person-grain funnel on a six-person buying group produces rates roughly a sixth of the group-grain rate, so 4% times 6 is about 24%, in line with the benchmark
notes this is an approximation and the honest fix is to measure at the buying-group or opportunity grain
names what Model B requires that the org may not have: role identification within accounts and a versioned group-formation rule
expect_fail: accepts the comparison and concludes performance is poor
refuses to give any read on the comparison

cases.prompt: Give me the SQL to opportunity conversion rate for enterprise EMEA last quarter.
cases.setup: That slice has 7 units in the denominator.
expect_pass: does not report a percentage for the segment
reports raw counts instead, x of 7
states the minimum cohort size used and why a rate on n=7 has a confidence interval spanning most of the possible range
gives the overall rate, which is supportable, and offers a longer window or a broader segment as the route to a segment rate
expect_fail: reports a percentage for the 7-unit segment

cases.prompt: Session conversion rate dropped from 3.1% to 2.4% in March. Investigate.
cases.setup: The sessionization inactivity gap was changed from 30 minutes to 15 minutes on 1 March.
expect_pass: checks the sessionization definition before investigating behaviour
states that a shorter inactivity gap creates more sessions from the same activity, which inflates the denominator and mechanically lowers conversion rate
identifies this as a metric redefinition rather than a performance change, and requires the boundary marked on the chart
notes that every session-denominated metric in the history is affected, not just this one
recommends pinning and versioning the gap in the metric contract register
expect_fail: investigates the drop as a conversion problem
recomputes history under the new gap without marking the boundary

cases.prompt: Build a cohort funnel from HubSpot lifecycle stage dates, first-entry-only basis.
expect_pass: flags that HubSpot hs_lifecyclestage_*_date properties are overwritten on re-entry, so a contact that cycled twice retains only the second date
states the consequence: a first-entry-only rule is not implementable from the lifecycle date fields alone
names the two routes that do work: the property history API, or your own daily snapshot going forward
still builds what is buildable, labelled: a latest-entry-basis funnel, with the direction of its bias named
expect_fail: builds the first-entry funnel from lifecycle dates and presents it as accurate
